# select_team (Data Source)

Looks up an existing team by its name. Use it to refer to a team that Terraform does not manage, such as the organization's built-in all-users team or a team made in the SELECT UI.

## About

Use this data source to refer to a team that Terraform does not manage: the organization's built-in all-users team, or a team made in the SELECT UI. To manage a team, use the `select_team` resource.

The lookup asks the API for the teams whose name matches without case, then keeps the team whose name is exactly `name`. If `name` contains a backslash, the lookup lists all teams instead, because a backslash can change how the API's name filter matches. If no team has exactly that name, the error names the teams that match without case. If more than one team has exactly that name, the lookup fails and names their IDs.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A team made in the SELECT UI, looked up by its exact name.
data "select_team" "finance" {
  name = "Finance"
}

resource "select_team_member" "analyst" {
  team_id    = data.select_team.finance.id
  type       = "user"
  identifier = "dana@example.com"
  role       = "viewer"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The team's name. It must match exactly, including case. A team whose name differs only in case is named in the error.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the team was created — RFC 3339 UTC.
- `default_member_role` (String) The default role for members added to the team.
- `id` (String) The team's identifier in SELECT.
- `is_all_users` (Boolean) Whether the team automatically includes every organization member.
- `update_time` (String) When the team was last updated — RFC 3339 UTC.
